newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks firmer, blue chips gain.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks firmer, blue chips gain.

text.p: Croatian stocks closed the week mostly firmer on Friday with notable gains in blue chips, and volume also rose as buyers came back for the last pre-Christmas session.
Traders said they did not expect much to happen in the two remaining trading days this year -- next Tuesday and Friday. The bourse is always closed Mondays.
"I expect foreign investors to become active early next year, but a stronger price increase is likely only late in February or March," Igor Kos of Taurus brokerage told Reuters.
Four of six traded issues rose, one fell and one was flat. But gains were limited to a range of 2.0-4.0 percent, which traders described as a one-off oscillation.
Fully-listed Zagrebacka banka was the biggest gainer and most actively traded issue with 6,094 shares sold.
It rose 4.08 percent to 1,020 kuna as its 1/10 GDRs traded at $19.25/62 in London, up from Thursday's close of $18.87.
Another blue chip, drugs firm Pliva, added 300 kuna or 2.25 percent to 13,600 kuna on volume of 666 units. Its GDR, issued at 50 to each share, also recovered to $51.62/87.
"These gains are within expected limits, but I believe Pliva will keep going up," Kos said.
Confectioner Kras and and food processor Podravka, which traders rank among the most promising issues, posted slight gains of 10 and five kuna to 410 and 210 kuna, respectively.
The only loser was cable maker Elka, 55 kuna down from last week to 140 kuna with 97 shares sold.
Volume more than doubled to 8,751 shares and turnover was 15.5 million kuna from Thursday's 5.8 million.
